Chapter 216 0213 China Celebrity List and Human Flesh Search

After the *History of Chinese Civilization* class, Chen Guilang pushed his bicycle, walking alongside Professor Xu Lai, who had just finished lecturing on the School of Principle of the Song and Ming dynasties.

"I've read the manuscript for *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* that you sent me," Professor Xu Lai said.

Chen Guilang asked, "Are there any mistakes in it?"

Professor Xu Lai commented, "No major issues. You must have read *The Case Records of Ming Scholars*, and also my book, *The Realm of Being and Non-being: The Spirit of Wang Yangming's Philosophy*. You've basically explained clearly the ideological changes during the reign of Emperor Wuzong of Ming, in conjunction with the social changes."

"As long as there are no major issues," Chen Guilang said with a smile.

Professor Xu Lai was somewhat dissatisfied, "But you've written it too superficially. You often just touch upon a point and move on, when you could actually delve a little deeper. You used a great deal of space to write about the gossipy anecdotes of people like Zhu Houzhao and Wang Yangming. Why not use some of that space to explore the School of Principle and the School of Mind a bit more deeply?"

Chen Guilang said with a smile, "No one would read it then. The general readership still prefers to read gossip. Discussing academic thought will just turn people away."

"Sigh, that's true too. You're writing popular science," Professor Xu Lai said.

Chen Guilang's version of *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* was projected to be nine volumes in total.

The first volume would end with the disappearance of the Jianwen Emperor.

The second volume would end with the Duomen Coup.

The third volume would end with the death of the Hongzhi Emperor from illness.

Particularly starting from Zhu Qizhen, the content written by Chen Guilang was vastly different from Dangnian Mingyue's version.

He did not glorify Zhu Qizhen, did not excessively denigrate Zhu Jianshen, nor did he excessively praise Zhu Youcheng. He wrote a lot of gossip about Imperial Consort Wan, but he didn't tear her to shreds. He also wrote about the love between Zhu Youcheng and Empress Zhang, but he equally wrote about the crappy things this couple did.

As for the upcoming fourth volume, why had Chen Guilang dragged it out for over a year before finishing?

The fifth volume, about the Jiajing era, would be even harder to write well.

Chen Guilang rode his bicycle to the library, copied some content from the *Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty*, then pushed his bike to a nearby cafeteria for lunch.

Back at the dorm, Chen Guilang organized his materials and turned on his computer to check his emails.

He hadn't gone to the company this morning, so his secretary had summarized some information and sent it directly to his inbox.

It was all information related to his competitors.

Ruolin Net had completely abandoned mass social networking and had transformed into a business website, no longer competing with Kaixin Net and Hainei Net.

Zhanzuo Net was still on life support, but there were recent rumors of a Series B funding round.

The real opponent was still the Korean-controlled Cyworld, whose registered users had already surpassed 1.2 million. Just in the middle of this month, Cyworld China launched Mobile Cyworld, and its "Cy-message" function was largely identical to "Weibo."

The truly big news was that Sina Blog had launched albums, friends, and follower functions yesterday!

Chen Guilang was trying to develop Kaixin Net's journals in the direction of blogs. And Sina Blog was also drawing inspiration from Kaixin Net, successively adding various social features.

It was a case of mutual convergence.

The blogosphere now had a triumvirate structure, with market shares as follows: Blog China 46%, Sina Blog 33%, and Sohu Blog 18%. Others 3%.

Chen Guilang opened all three major blogs and took a careful look.

Only Sina Blog was rapidly improving. Both Blog China and Sohu Blog currently did not allow adding friends or following bloggers.

The door was suddenly thrown open, and his roommates Li Heng and Tong Zhihong rushed in.

Li Heng sat down and immediately started writing something.

"What are you writing?" Chen Guilang asked.

Tong Zhihong, who was turning on his computer, said, "This guy has become a Party membership activist. He's writing his thought report in advance."

Li Heng chuckled, "I applied last semester. I didn't expect to become an activist this semester."

Chen Guilang sighed to himself; he wasn't qualified.

Because he had failed a course!

Familiar game music came from the speakers next to him; Tong Zhihong had already entered Stormwind City.

Sigh, this roommate of his had become obsessed with *World of Warcraft* and hadn't been playing much *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* lately.

His phone vibrated. Chen Guilang picked it up and saw it was a text message from Professor Wang: "I've finished reading your fourth volume manuscript. No historical errors. A few minor issues can be ignored."

Chen Guilang quickly replied, "Thank you, Professor Wang."

Professor Wang proactively asked, "Would you like me to help write a preface?"

"I couldn't ask for more," Chen Guilang said.

After confirming there were no issues with the manuscript, Chen Guilang finally emailed Li Xunhuan.

After handling all that, Chen Guilang heard the clatter of typing from next to him. Tong Zhihong had entered the game but wasn't playing, instead chatting with his in-game friends.

Soon, Tong Zhihong switched out of the game and went to the Mop Forum to look for a post.

"Bang!"

As he was reading, Tong Zhihong slammed the desk, saying indignantly, "This Tongxu is too despicable, an absolute scumbag."

Chen Guilang said, "Tongxu didn't do anything that bad, did he? He only killed his son-in-law."

Li Heng, who was writing his thought report, also asked curiously, "What's wrong?"

Tong Zhihong pointed at the Mop post and said, "There's a guild leader named Tongxu who slept with the wife of one of his guild members. And that woman, after getting married, does nothing all day but play games, and she even seduced her husband's guild leader. It's basically a modern-day Ximen Qing and Pan Jinlian!"

Li Heng's thoughts instantly went off-track, and he excitedly ran over to read the post and get in on the gossip.

Chen Guilang's memory was finally jogged: human flesh search!

The explosion of the Tongxu Gate incident gave the internet the term "human flesh search" for the first time.

Twenty years later, this phenomenon would be upgraded to "doxxing."

The "adulterer" was cyberbullied to the point where he couldn't function in daily life and became one of Baidu's Top Ten People of 2006.

Then, the "cuckold" admitted that he had made the story up...

Chen Guilang climbed back onto his bed for a nap. Li Heng immediately borrowed his computer to read the post, joining Tong Zhihong in furiously flaming the "adulterer."

Seeing their righteous indignation, Chen Guilang couldn't help but say, "Is it possible that this post is fake?"

Tong Zhihong said, "The QQ chat logs have been posted."

"Chat logs can be forged too," Chen Guilang said.

Tong Zhihong and Li Heng stopped their flaming. After some serious thought, they began to carefully examine the original post, and then studied the chat logs for any traces of Photoshop.

After a long while, Tong Zhihong said, "Let's wait for a follow-up. We really shouldn't be so rash."

Li Heng also temporarily set the matter aside. He switched to browsing news and quickly shouted, "Senior Chen, you made the Forbes China Celebrity List!"

Tong Zhihong asked, "What rank?"

Li Heng said, "Senior Chen is number 87. A total of four writers are on the list. Guo Xiaosi is number 64, Han Han is 79, and Yu Hua is 96."

"How is it ranked?" Tong Zhihong leaned over to study it with him.

This list was a comprehensive ranking based on career income, television exposure, newspaper exposure, web searches, and magazine covers.

The company stocks Chen Guilang held weren't even counted; only his royalties were roughly calculated.

Tong Zhihong said, "This ranking doesn't seem reasonable. A lot of models are on the list, and I don't know a single one of them. How can this be called the China Celebrity List?"

"I guess it's because models appear on fashion magazine covers more often," Li Heng analyzed.

After discussing for a while, the two went back to their own business.

After finishing the report and playing WoW, they took out their textbooks to prepare for the afternoon classes.

Li Heng was now a moderately famous parody uploader on Tudou, but he never showed his face. Because this guy was also a class officer, had joined the student union, was planning to join the Party, and had to get a scholarship every year.

According to Li Heng's plan, he might go into politics in the future.

Chen Guilang was drowsing through his afternoon nap when he felt the door open. He opened his eyes to see that Jiang Junlai was back.

Ever since this guy got a girlfriend, he spent less and less time in the dorm.

Chen Guilang got up with a yawn, went for a stroll downstairs, then pedaled his bicycle to the company.

On the way, his phone rang.

It was Li Xunhuan. "Boss Chen, you finally submitted the manuscript! You said you'd turn in two volumes by the end of last year, and you've dragged it out until now to give me just one?"

"The fifth volume is already in the works," Chen Guilang said.

Li Xunhuan said, "How about we publish it during the summer break? We can do a book signing then too."

"Sure, you arrange it," Chen Guilang said. "As for the promotion strategy, just pay attention to the news. ByteDance will have another round of financing this year, and it will be a huge amount."

Li Xunhuan laughed heartily, "The moment you get the VC funding, I'll start the promotion. It'll definitely sell like hotcakes, and we can boost the sales of the first three volumes at the same time!"

"Alright, hanging up now."

"Don't be so quick. I'll be back in Beijing in a couple of days. Let's get a meal together."

"Call me when you're here."

"I'll bring a few buddies. You guys can get to know each other. They're all famous, you can get them to register for accounts on Kaixin Net."

"That would be great. Who's coming?"

"Ning Caishen, Xing Yusen, and a few others. Those two guys are big shots now. The TV shows they wrote have very high ratings."

*My Own Swordsman* was currently a hit show, and Ning Caishen was especially popular right now.

The TV shows Xing Yusen was involved in were written by a team, including *Idler Ma's Sister*, *A Family in the Northeast*, *Home with Kids*, and so on.

Bringing them to Kaixin Net could potentially bring in many other screenwriters as well.

For the next few days, Chen Guilang waited for news every day.

The valuation of Bytely Tech by the venture capital firms had still not been finalized. This was mainly because their valuation methods differed, resulting in widely varying figures.

Moreover, *Reign of Hegemon* was still being continuously promoted.

As more and more whale players joined, the game's daily revenue became increasingly explosive!

On Thursday, the investment managers from several major firms held a meeting and decided they couldn't drag this on any longer.

The sooner they invested, the better.

Because a rumor had come from the US that Facebook's Series B financing was nearing its end. The post-money valuation was very likely to exceed 500 million US dollars.

The more glamorous Facebook was, the higher ByteDance's valuation would be, and there was no telling how many VC firms would be eyeing it.

On Friday, Li Xunhuan arrived in Beijing and called Chen Guilang, "CEO Chen, let's have dinner tonight!"

"Text me the address."

Just as he hung up, Chen Guilang received another call, this time from Zhang Suyang: "Mr. Chen, the VCs are coming to Beijing next week to formally begin the Series B financing negotiations."

(End of this chapter)
